why: People are nodes and every 1 in the matrix is an undirected edge; a friend circle is a connected component. Union-find merges each friendly pair, and the number of circles is n minus the number of successful merges.
hints: Indirect friendship is transitive: what graph concept is a 'friend circle'?
Count connected components. Start with n separate groups; each union of two different groups reduces the count by one.
Union-find with path compression over the upper triangle (j > i) of the matrix: O(n^2 * alpha(n)) for n <= 200. DFS from each unvisited person works equally well.
pitfalls: The diagonal is always 1; it is not an edge to anyone else.
The matrix is symmetric, so scanning only j > i avoids double work.
A person with no friends is still a circle of size 1.
